  "text": "On Thursday, Mara left the library at two. The atlas was back on its shelf, its repaired spine a shade darker than the others. Before going out, she checked the returns slot. It was empty.

The café across the street had six tables and a window that looked toward the library steps. Mara chose a table near the back. She ordered tea, then wished she had waited. By the time he arrived, a skin had formed on the milk in its little jug.

He stood in the doorway for a moment, looking around. His hair was thinner than she remembered. She raised her hand, and he came over with the careful walk she had noticed at the station years before, though she could not say whether his knee was worse.

He took off his coat. There was a loose thread at one cuff.

“I passed the library,” he said. “It’s smaller than I thought.”

“It hasn’t changed much.”

He ordered coffee. They spoke about the rain that was expected and the shop that had closed on the corner. When the waiter brought his cup, he moved the sugar bowl between them, though neither wanted any.

At last he asked if she had got home all right on Sunday. Mara said she had. She did not mention the suitcase, which was still beside the umbrella stand. That morning she had found the mark its wheel had made on the floor. In daylight it was easier to see, but she had stopped trying to rub it away."
